newsitem.title: DUBAI: Sudan accepts UAE mediation bid - minister.
newsitem.headline: Sudan accepts UAE mediation bid - minister.

text.p: Sudan has in principle accepted an offer by the United Arab Emirates to mediate an end to the African country's conflict, a Sudanese minister said in remarks published on Wednesday.

Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohammad Taha told the Arabic language Asharq al-Awsat newspaper Khartoum was waiting for the UAE to send a mediator to outline Abu Dhabi's plans before taking a final stand.

UAE President Sheikh Zaid Bin Sultan al-Nahayan told his Sudanese counterpart Omar Hassan al-Bashir last week the Gulf Arab state was willing to send an envoy to mediate in the rebel offensive launched a month ago from the south and east.

"Sudan has welcomed the intentions of Sheikh Zaid," Taha told the London-based daily. "But the official stand towards Sheikh Zaid's initiative will be defined in line with ideas and proposals carried by the envoy."
Officials have said the UAE is seeking support from other Arab countries for its mediation offer before it takes any moves to encourage dialogue with Sudan's Islamist-led government.
The Arab League has welcomed the UAE's efforts.
But the success of the initiative also hinged on reactions from the Sudanese opposition and Egypt.
Neither has given any clear response.

Though few Arab states appear sympathetic to Khartoum's Islamist government, most have said they backed Sudan's unity and sovereignty. Many, including Egypt, have indicated they would not intervene in what they consider an internal crisis.

Sudan has accused Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda of direct military involvement in the rebel offensive launched in early January by the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) and allied opposition forces. The three states deny any involvement.
